justification: All three round-1 blocking defects are verifiably fixed and none regressed. (1) Figure 1: the SVG source now starts every left-side annotation at x=65 ('referral: org's NS + glue' x2, 'answer, aa=1: a CNAME', the two-line closing caption), clear of the 'you' lifeline at x=55 by a 10-unit gap; confirmed visually in mobile-light part04 and mobile-dark part04 and in desktop-light part02 - no dashed line crosses any label in either theme at either width. (2) The record-type table is now three columns (Type, Stores, RFC 1035 RDATA merged/paraphrased into Type+Stores, with the RFC-quote column still present but scrolled off on a 390px phone); every visible Stores cell is a complete phrase ('IPv6 address (RFC 3596)', 'Alias to another name', 'Authoritative server for the zone', 'Mail server, with preference', 'Free-form text') with no mid-word truncation, a real change from round 1's 'not F...'/'instead...' clipping. A pixel-level crop of the table's right edge in both themes (mobile-light/dark part07-08) shows the shell's fade mask genuinely rendering - the table border and background visibly fade to transparent before the viewport edge - so a phone reader gets the 'there's more here' cue WRITER_GUIDE section 7 requires, not a hard clip. (3) The 'iana.org auth' loop was nudged from x=332 to x=324 and its label's right anchor moved from x=335 to x=338, opening an 11-unit-wider gap; confirmed in both mobile themes and on desktop that the loop curve no longer touches the label. A fresh full pass over headings (five plain H2s matching the on-page TOC, no skipped levels), the two exercise/solution collapses (both render collapsed with a working 'Show solution' toggle, no leaked answers, correct accent coloring in both themes), the sources/footer/related-articles block, and the remaining prose/code sections turned up no new issues. The one substantive gap still open is the one this round was explicitly told not to touch: the BuildQuery/ReadName pair is still retyped in full four times (id=walk at ~139 lines, the exercise-1 solution, id=records, and the exercise-2 solution), and the article's only figure still sits at roughly the 20% mark, leaving the record-type, TTL and failure-mode sections - most of the page - as unbroken text and code. That is unchanged from round 1, was flagged there as a writer-owned major, and remains the reason this article is not yet at the pass bar: it is a real, still-uncorrected cost to reading rhythm on a 2997-word, 14-code-block page, independent of the three defects this round fixed. The round-1 minor about Figure 1 being visually undersized on wide desktop viewports (a ~410px drawing inside a ~735px frame) is also unchanged, confirmed present in desktop-light part02; it remains shared shell CSS (`.diagram-scroll > svg` sizing), owner integrator, not a writer defect and not blocking on its own.
